newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares ease on National Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares ease on National Stock Exchange.

text.p: Share prices weakened on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday largely because of lack of support from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), dealers said.

"Normally, Monday is the first day (of new account) on the NSE," said the chief dealer at a Bombay brokerage. Normal trading on the BSE would begin only at 1400 hours (0830 gmt) on Monday as a postponed badla (carryforward) session is being held in the morning, exchange officials said.
"Operators are having a field day pushing down prices, especially those in the no-delivery section," said a trader. He said this was possible because of lack of suport from the BSE.
"But once the BSE opens, I expect NSE to firm," he said.
Shares of Indian tobacco major ITC Ltd lost over 5.0 percent on NSE largely on reports of an enquiry into a $110 million foreign exchange violation case, dealers said.
But others said this was only an excuse, as the case has been simmering for many months.
Other blue-chips which lost in early NSE trade were SBI, Reliance, Tata Steel, Tata Tea, TELCO, Bank of India and BSES.
The NSE index lost 16.85 points or 1.38 percent at 1,206.65 in early trade.
